title: Equal and Not Equal: Balances and Fair Sharing
seo_title: Kindergarten Equal and not equal Worksheets: Free Math with Pictures and Answers (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Equality and inequality as a balance: modeling equality as balanced and inequality as imbalanced using concrete and visual models; fish drying and sharing
meta_desc: Free Kindergarten math worksheets on equal and not equal for the BC curriculum: pan balances, which side has more, making a balance, equal groups and fair sharing stories. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_big: Equal amounts make a balance level.
key_sub: If one side has more, it goes down. Add to the lighter side or take from the heavier side to balance.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A pan scale is balanced (level) when both sides have the same amount. The sides are equal.
  • When one side has more, that side goes down. The sides are not equal.
  • To make a scale balance, add to the side with fewer, or take some off the side with more.

Examples

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Thinking the higher side has moreThe side with more is heavier and goes down.
Giving the bigger number for how many to addFind how many more the heavier side has.
Thinking groups are equal because they look as wideCount both groups.

faq.q: What does equality as a balance mean?
faq.a: Two amounts are equal when a pan balance is level. If one side has more, it goes down and the amounts are not equal.

faq.q: How can I show equal and not equal at home?
faq.a: Use a coat hanger with two cups, or line up two rows of toys and count each row.
Sharing so that everyone gets an equal amount, like putting the same number of fish on each drying rack.

faq.q: Do Kindergarten children use the = sign?
faq.a: They start with the words equal and not equal and with balances. The = and ≠ symbols come in Grade 1.
